answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy arises when each identity must bind to a scarce physical copper token whose possession is proven on-chain. Agents are obliged to wander through a live lagoon simulation fed by independent sensor oracles; only the true copper holder can generate timely signed attestations matching the real-time water data. Attackers face linear costs in metal acquisition and cannot cheaply multiplex one sensor stream across many fake agents, rendering large-scale identity farming uneconomical.
